claim: Tns3 is a direct target gene of Olig2, Chd7, and Chd8 transcriptional regulators of oligodendrocyte differentiation.
source: Here, we show that the regulator of focal adhesion, Tensin3 (Tns3), is a direct target gene of Olig2, Chd7, and Chd8, transcriptional regulators of OL differentiation.
evidence: Supported by ChIP-seq data showing Olig2, Chd7, and Chd8 binding to Tns3 promoters (Figure 1e) and transcriptome analysis showing Tns3 downregulation upon Chd7 and Chd8 deletion (Figure 1f, g).

claim: Tns3 is transiently upregulated in immature oligodendrocytes.
source: Tns3 is transiently upregulated and localized to cell processes of immature OLs, together with integrin-β1, a key mediator of survival at this transient stage.
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence showing Tns3 protein in CC1+ iOLs (Figure 2a-e) and scRNA-seq showing high Tns3 transcript levels in iOL clusters (Figure 1—figure supplement 2d, e).

claim: Constitutive Tns3 loss of function leads to reduced viability in mouse and humans.
source: Constitutive Tns3 loss of function leads to reduced viability in mouse and humans, with surviving knockout mice still expressing Tns3 in oligodendroglia.
evidence: Supported by analysis of Tns3 knockout mice showing developmental lethality (Figure 3—figure supplement 1k, l) and gnomAD data showing TNS3 loss-of-function variants cause ~80% developmental mortality in humans (Figure 3—figure supplement 2a).

claim: Acute deletion of Tns3 in postnatal neural stem cells leads to a twofold reduction in oligodendrocyte numbers.
source: Acute deletion of Tns3 in vivo, either in postnatal neural stem cells (NSCs) or in OPCs, leads to a twofold reduction in OL numbers.
evidence: Demonstrated by CRISPR-mediated Tns3 deletion in P1 NSCs showing ~50% reduction in GFP+ OLs at P22 (Figure 3c, c', d).

claim: Acute deletion of Tns3 in oligodendrocyte precursor cells leads to a twofold reduction in oligodendrocyte numbers.
source: Acute deletion of Tns3 in vivo, either in postnatal neural stem cells (NSCs) or in OPCs, leads to a twofold reduction in OL numbers.
evidence: Demonstrated by tamoxifen-induced Tns3 deletion in OPCs showing 38-51% reduction in OL density across brain regions (Figure 4b-d).

claim: Transient upregulation of Tns3 protects differentiating OPCs and immature OLs from cell death by preventing p53 upregulation.
source: We find that the transient upregulation of Tns3 is required to protect differentiating OPCs and immature OLs from cell death by preventing the upregulation of p53, a key regulator of apoptosis.
evidence: Supported by TUNEL assays showing fivefold increase in apoptotic cells in Tns3-iKO brains (Figure 5a-c) and immunofluorescence showing tenfold increase in p53+ OPCs and fourfold increase in p53+ iOLs in Tns3-iKO (Figure 6a-c).

claim: Olig2, Chd7, and Chd8 commonly bind three putative promoters of Tns3 with active transcription marks in purified oligodendroglia.
source: Indeed, Olig2, Chd7, and Chd8 commonly bound three putative promoters of Tns3 having active transcription marks in purified oligodendroglia (H3K27ac/H3K24me3; Figure 1e).
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-seq tracks showing co-binding of Olig2, Chd7, and Chd8 at Tns3 promoter regions with H3K27ac and H3K4me3 marks (Figure 1e).

claim: Tns3 transcripts are largely downregulated upon acute deletion of Chd7 in postnatal OPCs/iOLs.
source: Tns3 transcripts were largely downregulated upon acute deletion of these factors in postnatal OPCs/iOLs (Figure 1f and g), indicating that Tns3 expression in OPCs/iOLs is directly controlled by Chd7 and Chd8 chromatin remodelers, key regulators of OL differentiation.
evidence: Shown by RNA-seq data comparing Chd7iKO and control O4+ cells (Figure 1f).

claim: Tns3 transcripts are largely downregulated upon acute deletion of Chd8 in postnatal OPCs/iOLs.
source: Tns3 transcripts were largely downregulated upon acute deletion of these factors in postnatal OPCs/iOLs (Figure 1f and g), indicating that Tns3 expression in OPCs/iOLs is directly controlled by Chd7 and Chd8 chromatin remodelers, key regulators of OL differentiation.
evidence: Shown by RNA-seq data comparing Chd8cKO and control O4+ cells (Figure 1g).

claim: Tns3 shows the highest expression levels in immature oligodendrocytes relative to other brain cell types.
source: Among these genes, Tns3 coding for Tensin3, a focal adhesion protein deregulated in certain cancers (Martuszewska et al., 2009), showed the highest expression levels in iOLs relative to other brain cell types (Zhang et al., 2014; Figure 1d).
evidence: Demonstrated by heatmap analysis of 794 genes showing Tns3 as the third most specific to iOLs compared to other cell types (Figure 1d), citing published dataset from Zhang et al., 2014.

claim: Tns3 protein is detected at high levels in the cytoplasm and main processes of CC1+ immature oligodendrocytes but not in their nuclei.
source: We then characterized Tns3 protein expression in oligodendroglia using V5 antibodies, finding that Tns3 protein can be detected at high levels in the cytoplasm and main processes of CC1+ iOLs but not in their nuclei (Figure 2a).
evidence: Shown by immunofluorescence using V5 antibodies in Tns3Tns3-V5 mice (Figure 2a).

claim: Tns3 largely overlaps with Itpr2, a suggested immature oligodendrocyte marker.
source: Using an antibody recognizing Itpr2, a suggested iOL marker (Marques et al., 2016), we saw that Tns3 largely overlapped with Itpr2 (Figure 2b).
evidence: Demonstrated by co-immunofluorescence showing overlap of Tns3-V5 and Itpr2 in CC1+ cells (Figure 2b), citing Marques et al., 2016 for Itpr2 as iOL marker.

claim: High levels of Tns3 are found in iOL1s (Nkx2.2+/Olig1- cells) and a fraction of iOL2s (Nkx2.2-/Olig1cytoplamic cells).
source: Using Nkx2.2 and Olig1cytoplamic expression distinguishing iOL1 and iOL2, respectively, we found high levels of Tns3 in iOL1s (Nkx2.2+/Olig1- cells) and a fraction of iOL2s (Nkx2.2-/Olig1cytoplamic cells; Figure 2c, i and j), suggesting that Tns3 protein expression peaks in early iOLs.
evidence: Shown by immunofluorescence with Nkx2.2, Olig1, and Tns3-V5 antibodies and quantification (Figure 2c, i, j).

claim: Tns3 levels decrease with increasing levels of Opalin, with Tns3-V5 levels undetectable in myelinating oligodendrocytes.
source: Comparison with Opalin protein localized in the cell body, processes, and myelin segments of OLs showed that Tns3 levels decreased with increasing levels of Opalin, with Tns3-V5 levels undetectable in myelinating OLs (i.e., Opalin+/CC1+ cells presenting myelinated segments; Figure 2d, arrowheads).
evidence: Demonstrated by co-immunofluorescence of Tns3-V5, Opalin, and CC1 (Figure 2d).

claim: Both full-length (155 kDa) and short (61 kDa) Tns3 isoforms are detected in O4+ cells from P7 and P14 brains but not at P21.
source: Indeed, we could detect both the full-length (1450 aa, 155 kDa) and the Tns3 short (C-term, 61 kDa) isoforms in O4+ cells from brains at P7 and P14 stages having many iOLs, but not at P21 having mainly mOLs (Figure 2—figure supplement 2g and h), thus validating the specificity of the anti-V5 antibodies in recognizing Tns3 protein.
evidence: Shown by Western blot analysis using V5 antibodies in MACSorted O4+ cells from Tns3Tns3-V5 mice at different postnatal stages (Figure 2—figure supplement 2g, h).

claim: TNS3 is highly expressed in human immature oligodendrocytes differentiated from iPSCs.
source: Cells expressing high levels of TNS3 corresponded to iOLs (iOL1 and iOL2 clusters, Figure 1—figure supplement 2g and h).
evidence: Demonstrated by scRNA-seq analysis of human oligodendroglia differentiated from embryonic stem cells showing TNS3 expression in iOL clusters (Figure 1—figure supplement 2f-h), citing Chamling et al., 2021 dataset.

claim: TNS3 expression pattern is conserved between mouse and human oligodendrogenesis.
source: We obtained similar results analyzing a human fetal midterm cerebellum (GW9-GW22) dataset (Aldinger et al., 2021), with high levels of TNS3 in iOLs similar to other suggested iOL markers such as ITPR2, ENPP6, and BCAS1, indicating a conserved expression pattern of Tns3/TNS3 between mouse and human oligodendrogenesis (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Shown by analysis of human fetal cerebellum scRNA-seq data showing TNS3 expression in iOL clusters (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), citing Aldinger et al., 2021 dataset.

claim: Tns3 is expressed in newly formed oligodendrocytes during remyelination.
source: We found that while non-lesioned adult brain regions contained only sparse Tns3+ iOLs (CC1high/Olig1cyto-high cells), remarkably many Tns3+ iOLs were detected in the remyelinating area using both V5 (Figure 2—figure supplement 4a and c, arrows) and Tns3 antibodies (Figure 2—figure supplement 4b, arrows).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence in lysolecithin-induced demyelinating lesions showing increased Tns3+ iOLs around lesion borders (Figure 2—figure supplement 4a-d).

claim: Tns3 expression is detected in some microglia/macrophages in demyelinating lesion areas.
source: Of note, we could also detect Tns3 expression in some microglia/macrophages in the lesion area using a combination of F4/80 antibodies (Figure 2—figure supplement 4c, arrowheads).
evidence: Shown by co-immunofluorescence of Tns3 and F4/80 in remyelinating lesions (Figure 2—figure supplement 4c).

claim: CRISPR-mediated Tns3 deletion in neonatal NSCs leads to no changes in the proportion of GFP+ OPCs.
source: Remarkably, brains electroporated with the CRISPR plasmids targeting Tns3 had a twofold reduction in GFP+ OLs compared to brains electroporated with control plasmids, while GFP+ OPCs were found in similar proportions (Figure 3c, c' and d).
evidence: Demonstrated by quantification of GFP+ cell types at P22 after P1 electroporation showing no change in OPC proportion (Figure 3c, c', d).

claim: CRISPR-mediated Tns3 deletion in neonatal NSCs leads to a 1.5-fold increase in the proportion of GFP+ astrocytes.
source: The proportion of GFP+ astrocytes was increased by 1.5-fold, likely as a result of the large reduction in OLs, as the number of GFP+ astrocytes was not changed (61.3 ± 10.9 in experimental versus 57.2 ± 11.8 in controls; Figure 3c, c' and d).
evidence: Shown by quantification of GFP+ cell types showing increased astrocyte proportion but unchanged absolute numbers (Figure 3c, c', d).

claim: Loss of Tns3 does not affect OPC generation at P11.
source: We found no differences in the proportion of GFP cells being OPCs (Figure 3e), nor the proliferative status of GFP+ OPCs (MCM2+/PDGFRα+ cells; Figure 3f) between experimental and control brains, while the reduction of OLs was already marked (Figure 3e), indicating that loss of Tns3 only affected the process of OPC differentiation into OLs.
evidence: Demonstrated by quantification at P11 showing similar OPC proportions between Tns3-deleted and control conditions (Figure 3e).

claim: Loss of Tns3 does not affect OPC proliferation at P11.
source: We found no differences in the proportion of GFP cells being OPCs (Figure 3e), nor the proliferative status of GFP+ OPCs (MCM2+/PDGFRα+ cells; Figure 3f) between experimental and control brains, while the reduction of OLs was already marked (Figure 3e), indicating that loss of Tns3 only affected the process of OPC differentiation into OLs.
evidence: Shown by quantification of MCM2+ proliferative OPCs showing no difference between conditions (Figure 3f).

claim: Deletion of both Tns3 isoforms has a similar impact on OL differentiation as deletion of only full-length Tns3.
source: We found a similar reduction of OLs in the loss of the two Tns3 isoforms than in mutations affecting only full-length Tns3 (Figure 3h, h' and i), suggesting that the small Tns3 isoform does not play an additional role with full-length Tns3 in OL formation.
evidence: Demonstrated by comparing OL reduction in 5'-3' gRNA deletion versus single gRNA deletion experiments (Figure 3h, h', i).

claim: Tamoxifen-induced Tns3 deletion in OPCs leads to 38.95% reduction in OLs in the corpus callosum.
source: Remarkably, the number of OLs (CC1+/GFP+ cells) was reduced by half in all quantified regions (reduction of 38.95% in the CC, 48.60% in cortex, 50.88% in the fimbria, 38% in the striatum; Figure 4b–d, Figure 4—figure supplement 2e–f', Figure 4—figure supplement 3b and b') in Tns3-iKO compared to control, while OPC (PDGFRα+/GFP+ cells) density was unchanged (Figure 4b–d).
evidence: Shown by quantification of CC1+ OLs in corpus callosum of Tns3-iKO versus control mice (Figure 4b-d).

claim: Tamoxifen-induced Tns3 deletion in OPCs leads to 48.60% reduction in OLs in the cortex.
source: Remarkably, the number of OLs (CC1+/GFP+ cells) was reduced by half in all quantified regions (reduction of 38.95% in the CC, 48.60% in cortex, 50.88% in the fimbria, 38% in the striatum; Figure 4b–d, Figure 4—figure supplement 2e–f', Figure 4—figure supplement 3b and b') in Tns3-iKO compared to control, while OPC (PDGFRα+/GFP+ cells) density was unchanged (Figure 4b–d).
evidence: Shown by quantification of CC1+ OLs in cortex of Tns3-iKO versus control mice (Figure 4c, d).

claim: Tamoxifen-induced Tns3 deletion in OPCs leads to 50.88% reduction in OLs in the fimbria.
source: Remarkably, the number of OLs (CC1+/GFP+ cells) was reduced by half in all quantified regions (reduction of 38.95% in the CC, 48.60% in cortex, 50.88% in the fimbria, 38% in the striatum; Figure 4b–d, Figure 4—figure supplement 2e–f', Figure 4—figure supplement 3b and b') in Tns3-iKO compared to control, while OPC (PDGFRα+/GFP+ cells) density was unchanged (Figure 4b–d).
evidence: Shown by quantification of CC1+ OLs in fimbria of Tns3-iKO versus control mice (Figure 4b, d).

claim: Tamoxifen-induced Tns3 deletion in OPCs leads to 38% reduction in OLs in the striatum.
source: Remarkably, the number of OLs (CC1+/GFP+ cells) was reduced by half in all quantified regions (reduction of 38.95% in the CC, 48.60% in cortex, 50.88% in the fimbria, 38% in the striatum; Figure 4b–d, Figure 4—figure supplement 2e–f', Figure 4—figure supplement 3b and b') in Tns3-iKO compared to control, while OPC (PDGFRα+/GFP+ cells) density was unchanged (Figure 4b–d).
evidence: Shown by quantification of CC1+ OLs in striatum of Tns3-iKO versus control mice (Figure 4d).

claim: Tns3 deletion does not change OPC density in the postnatal brain.
source: Remarkably, the number of OLs (CC1+/GFP+ cells) was reduced by half in all quantified regions (reduction of 38.95% in the CC, 48.60% in cortex, 50.88% in the fimbria, 38% in the striatum; Figure 4b–d, Figure 4—figure supplement 2e–f', Figure 4—figure supplement 3b and b') in Tns3-iKO compared to control, while OPC (PDGFRα+/GFP+ cells) density was unchanged (Figure 4b–d).
evidence: Demonstrated by quantification showing similar PDGFRα+ OPC density in Tns3-iKO and control across brain regions (Figure 4b-d).

claim: The density of iOL1s (Nkx2.2high cells) is unchanged in Tns3-iKO compared to controls.
source: Using markers distinguishing different stages of OL differentiation (iOL1 and iOL2/mOL), we found that the density of iOL1s (Nkx2.2high cells), which express the highest levels of Tns3 protein in control brains, was unchanged (Figure 4—figure supplement 2b,b',d), while the density of early iOL2s (CC1+/Olig1- cells) and later OL stages (iOL2/mOLs CC1+/Olig1+ cells) was reduced by 30 and 50%, respectively, in Tns3-iKO compared to controls (Figure 4e–f), suggesting that Tns3 is required for normal OL differentiation.
evidence: Shown by quantification of Nkx2.2high iOL1s showing no change in density (Figure 4—figure supplement 2b, b', d).

claim: The density of early iOL2s (CC1+/Olig1- cells) is reduced by 30% in Tns3-iKO compared to controls.
source: Using markers distinguishing different stages of OL differentiation (iOL1 and iOL2/mOL), we found that the density of iOL1s (Nkx2.2high cells), which express the highest levels of Tns3 protein in control brains, was unchanged (Figure 4—figure supplement 2b,b',d), while the density of early iOL2s (CC1+/Olig1- cells) and later OL stages (iOL2/mOLs CC1+/Olig1+ cells) was reduced by 30 and 50%, respectively, in Tns3-iKO compared to controls (Figure 4e–f), suggesting that Tns3 is required for normal OL differentiation.
evidence: Demonstrated by quantification of CC1+/Olig1- iOL2s showing ~30% reduction (Figure 4e-f).

claim: The density of later OL stages (iOL2/mOLs CC1+/Olig1+ cells) is reduced by 50% in Tns3-iKO compared to controls.
source: Using markers distinguishing different stages of OL differentiation (iOL1 and iOL2/mOL), we found that the density of iOL1s (Nkx2.2high cells), which express the highest levels of Tns3 protein in control brains, was unchanged (Figure 4—figure supplement 2b,b',d), while the density of early iOL2s (CC1+/Olig1- cells) and later OL stages (iOL2/mOLs CC1+/Olig1+ cells) was reduced by 30 and 50%, respectively, in Tns3-iKO compared to controls (Figure 4e–f), suggesting that Tns3 is required for normal OL differentiation.
evidence: Shown by quantification of CC1+/Olig1+ iOL2/mOLs showing ~50% reduction (Figure 4e-f).

claim: Tns3 deletion does not significantly change OPC proliferation in the postnatal brain.
source: Finally, we assessed possible changes in OPC proliferation by immunodetection of Mcm2, finding no significant changes in the proliferation of Tns3-iKO OPCs compared to control OPCs (Figure 4—figure supplement 3c,c',d).
evidence: Demonstrated by quantification of MCM2+ proliferative OPCs showing no significant difference (Figure 4—figure supplement 3c, c', d).

claim: There is a fivefold increase in TUNEL+ cells in the dorsal telencephalon of Tns3-iKO brain compared to control.
source: Interestingly, we found a fivefold increase in TUNEL+ cells in the dorsal telencephalon of Tns3-iKO brain, compared to control, without significant changes in non-oligodendroglial cells present in the SVZ (Figure 5a–c).
evidence: Shown by TUNEL assay quantification in P21 Tns3-iKO versus control brains (Figure 5a-c).

claim: Tns3-deleted oligodendroglia show a fourfold increase in probability to die compared to control cells in culture.
source: Live-imaging monitoring of cell behavior showed that once YFP+ cells had developed multiple branched morphology, characteristic of differentiating OLs, they showed a fourfold increase in their probability to die compared to YFP− cells of the same culture (Figure 5f–h, yellow and white arrows, respectively) or to cells from control cultures, with more pronounced cell death by the third day of culture (Figure 5f and g).
evidence: Demonstrated by video microscopy quantification showing increased cell death of YFP+ Tns3-iKO cells versus YFP- or control cells (Figure 5f-h).

claim: There is a tenfold increase in p53+ OPCs (GFP+/CC1- cells) in Tns3-iKO compared to control.
source: Interestingly, we found a tenfold increase in p53+ OPCs (GFP+/CC1- cells) and fourfold increase in p53+ iOLs (GFP+/CC1+ cells) in Tns3-iKO compared to control (Figure 6a–c), suggesting that the loss of Tns3 leads to an upregulation of p53, which, together with the loss of integrin-β1 survival signal, mediates the cell death of Tns3-iKO differentiating oligodendroglia (Figure 6d).
evidence: Shown by immunofluorescence quantification of p53+ cells in Tns3-iKO versus control brains (Figure 6a-c).

claim: There is a fourfold increase in p53+ iOLs (GFP+/CC1+ cells) in Tns3-iKO compared to control.
source: Interestingly, we found a tenfold increase in p53+ OPCs (GFP+/CC1- cells) and fourfold increase in p53+ iOLs (GFP+/CC1+ cells) in Tns3-iKO compared to control (Figure 6a–c), suggesting that the loss of Tns3 leads to an upregulation of p53, which, together with the loss of integrin-β1 survival signal, mediates the cell death of Tns3-iKO differentiating oligodendroglia (Figure 6d).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence quantification of p53+ OLs in Tns3-iKO versus control brains (Figure 6a-c).

claim: Tns3-iKO oligodendroglia show 2082 differentially expressed genes compared to control.
source: Statistical analyses using edgeR (Chen et al., 2016) showed 2082 differentially expressed genes (DEGs, p-value<0.05) between Tns3-iKO and control, with 834 downregulated and 1248 upregulated genes (Figure 7b).
evidence: Shown by RNA-seq analysis of MACSorted O4+ cells from Tns3-iKO and control brains (Figure 7b), citing Chen et al., 2016 for edgeR method.

claim: Main downregulated processes in Tns3-iKO oligodendroglia include gliogenesis, glial cell differentiation, oligodendrocyte differentiation, and lipid metabolism.
source: Gene Ontology (GO) analysis of biological processes indicated that main downregulated processes were involved in terms related OL differentiation (including gliogenesis, glial cell differentiation, OL differentiation, lipid metabolism, and positive regulation of cell projection organization; Figure 7c and e, Supplementary file 1), while the upregulated biological processes related to terms such as cellular stress and p53 pathway (including double-strand break repair, cellular response to oxidative stress, and signal transduction of p53 class mediator), opposite processes involved in cell cycle regulation (including DNA integrity check point, G2/M transition of mitotic cell cycle, and positive- and negative regulation of cell cycle process) (Figure 7d, f and g, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Demonstrated by GO analysis of downregulated genes in Tns3-iKO O4+ cells (Figure 7c, e).

claim: Upregulated biological processes in Tns3-iKO oligodendroglia include cellular stress, p53 pathway, and cell cycle regulation terms.
source: Gene Ontology (GO) analysis of biological processes indicated that main downregulated processes were involved in terms related OL differentiation (including gliogenesis, glial cell differentiation, OL differentiation, lipid metabolism, and positive regulation of cell projection organization; Figure 7c and e, Supplementary file 1), while the upregulated biological processes related to terms such as cellular stress and p53 pathway (including double-strand break repair, cellular response to oxidative stress, and signal transduction of p53 class mediator), opposite processes involved in cell cycle regulation (including DNA integrity check point, G2/M transition of mitotic cell cycle, and positive- and negative regulation of cell cycle process) (Figure 7d, f and g, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Shown by GO analysis of upregulated genes in Tns3-iKO O4+ cells (Figure 7d, f, g).

claim: GO processes related to integrin signaling and cell adhesion are upregulated in Tns3-iKO oligodendroglia.
source: Interestingly, GO processes related to integrin signaling and cell adhesion were upregulated (including positive regulation of cell adhesion, regulation of cell adhesion mediated by integrin, integrin-mediated signaling pathway, and positive regulation of cell adhesion; Figure 7d, Supplementary file 1), with several integrin transcripts upregulated (Itgam, Itga8, Itgb2, Itga4, Itgb3, Itgb5, Itga6, Itgb8, which are normally not expressed in OPCs/iOLs; Supplementary file 1), while Fyn, Src family kinase that associates with α6β1 and is required to amplify PDGF survival signaling (Colognato et al., 2004) was downregulated (1.4-fold, p-value=0.03; Supplementary file 1), suggesting that Tns3 deletion impairs normal integrin signaling, and as a consequence Tns3-deleted cells try to compensate this impairment upregulating of other integrin family members.
evidence: Demonstrated by GO analysis and gene expression data showing upregulation of integrin-related processes and genes (Figure 7d), citing Colognato et al., 2004 for Fyn function.

claim: Fyn is downregulated 1.4-fold in Tns3-iKO oligodendroglia.
source: Interestingly, GO processes related to integrin signaling and cell adhesion were upregulated (including positive regulation of cell adhesion, regulation of cell adhesion mediated by integrin, integrin-mediated signaling pathway, and positive regulation of cell adhesion; Figure 7d, Supplementary file 1), with several integrin transcripts upregulated (Itgam, Itga8, Itgb2, Itga4, Itgb3, Itgb5, Itga6, Itgb8, which are normally not expressed in OPCs/iOLs; Supplementary file 1), while Fyn, Src family kinase that associates with α6β1 and is required to amplify PDGF survival signaling (Colognato et al., 2004) was downregulated (1.4-fold, p-value=0.03; Supplementary file 1), suggesting that Tns3 deletion impairs normal integrin signaling, and as a consequence Tns3-deleted cells try to compensate this impairment upregulating of other integrin family members.
evidence: Shown by RNA-seq data analysis, citing Colognato et al., 2004 for Fyn function in PDGF survival signaling.

claim: Tns3 and integrin-β1 co-localize in CNP+ differentiating oligodendrocytes in culture.
source: Furthermore, using neural progenitor differentiation cultures, we observed co-expression of integrin-β1 and Tns3 in CNP+ OLs by immunofluorescence (Figure 5—figure supplement 1c), suggesting that Tns3 could relay integrin-β1-mediated survival signal in differentiating oligodendroglia.
evidence: Demonstrated by co-immunofluorescence in neural progenitor cultures (Figure 5—figure supplement 1c).

claim: Tns3 expression pattern in iOLs closely matches that of Itgb1 (integrin-β1), Fyn, Bcar1/p130Cas, and Ptk2/Fak in mouse and human oligodendroglia.
source: Indeed, Tns3 expression pattern in iOLs was closely matching that of Itgb1 (integrin-b1), Fyn, Bcar1/p130Cas, and Ptk2/Fak both in mouse and human oligodendroglia (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a and b).
evidence: Shown by dot plot analysis of scRNA-seq data from mouse and human oligodendroglia (Figure 5—figure supplement 1a, b).

claim: Olig2 binds 16,578 chromatin sites corresponding to 8,672 genes in O4+ oligodendroglial cells.
source: Among the 16,578 chromatin sites bound by Olig2 corresponding to 8672 genes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d), there were key regulators of OL differentiation, including Ascl1, Sox10, Myrf, Chd8, and Smarca4/Brg1 (Figure 1b; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-seq analysis in MACSorted O4+ cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d).

claim: Olig2 binds promoters (60%) and enhancers (40%) in oligodendroglial cells.
source: The profile of activity histone marks at Olig2-binding sites indicated that Olig2 binds promoters (60%) and enhancers (40%) with either active or more poised/repressive states (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a–f), supporting the suggested pioneer function of Olig2 in oligodendrogenesis (Yu et al., 2013).
evidence: Shown by analysis of Olig2 ChIP-seq data with histone marks (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a-f), citing Yu et al., 2013 for Olig2 pioneer function.

claim: 1,774 chromatin sites are commonly bound by Olig2, Chd7, and Chd8 in oligodendroglial cells.
source: Combining Olig2 with Chd7 and Chd8 binding profiles, which we previously generated using the same protocol (Marie et al., 2018), we found 1774 chromatin sites commonly bound by the three regulators, with half of them (47% and 832 peaks) corresponding to active promoters (H3K4me3/H3K27ac marks) of 654 protein-coding genes (Figure 1c, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Demonstrated by integration of ChIP-seq datasets (Figure 1c), citing Marie et al., 2018 for Chd7 and Chd8 ChIP-seq data.

claim: 832 peaks commonly bound by Olig2, Chd7, and Chd8 correspond to active promoters of 654 protein-coding genes.
source: Combining Olig2 with Chd7 and Chd8 binding profiles, which we previously generated using the same protocol (Marie et al., 2018), we found 1774 chromatin sites commonly bound by the three regulators, with half of them (47% and 832 peaks) corresponding to active promoters (H3K4me3/H3K27ac marks) of 654 protein-coding genes (Figure 1c, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Shown by ChIP-seq analysis combining Olig2, Chd7, and Chd8 binding data (Figure 1c), citing Marie et al., 2018.

claim: Olig2 binds key regulators of OL differentiation including Ascl1, Sox10, Myrf, Chd8, and Smarca4/Brg1.
source: Among the 16,578 chromatin sites bound by Olig2 corresponding to 8672 genes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1d), there were key regulators of OL differentiation, including Ascl1, Sox10, Myrf, Chd8, and Smarca4/Brg1 (Figure 1b; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-seq tracks showing Olig2 binding at these gene loci (Figure 1b).

claim: Tns3 is the main Tensin expressed in oligodendroglia compared to Tns1 and Tns2.
source: Finally, we investigated whether other Tensin family members were expressed in oligodendroglia, finding that Tns1 and Tns2 but not Tns4 were detectable at low levels in iOLs by immunofluorescence (Figure 2—figure supplement 3a and b), paralleling their low transcription levels compared to Tns3 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3c; brainrnaseq.org). Therefore, Tns3 appears to be the main Tensin expressed during OL differentiation, suggesting that Tns3 function in iOLs is likely to be evolutionarily selected, and thus of biological importance in oligodendrogenesis.
evidence: Shown by immunofluorescence and transcript expression data comparing Tns1, Tns2, and Tns3 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3a-c).

claim: Tns4 is not detectable in immature oligodendrocytes.
source: Finally, we investigated whether other Tensin family members were expressed in oligodendroglia, finding that Tns1 and Tns2 but not Tns4 were detectable at low levels in iOLs by immunofluorescence (Figure 2—figure supplement 3a and b), paralleling their low transcription levels compared to Tns3 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3c; brainrnaseq.org).
evidence: Stated based on immunofluorescence analysis.

claim: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants of TNS3 cause approximately 80% developmental mortality in the human population.
source: Homozygous predicted loss-of-function (pLoF) alleles of TNS3 were not found, and heterozygous pLoF were greatly below the expected frequency (0.1 observed/expected ratio, with 90% CI of 0.05–0.19; and LOEUF of 0.19; Figure 3—figure supplement 2a; https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org), meaning that heterozygous loss-of-function variants of TNS3 cause ~80% developmental mortality, a rate similarly high to key neurodevelopmental genes such as SOX10 (LOEUF = 0.21; Figure 3—figure supplement 2b), CHD7 (LOEUF = 0.08; Figure 3—figure supplement 2c), and CHD8 (LOEUF = 0.08; Figure 3—figure supplement 2d), contrary to less broadly required factors such as NKX2-2 (LOEUF = 0.67; Figure 3—figure supplement 2e) and OLIG1 (LOEUF = 1.08; Figure 3—figure supplement 2f).
evidence: Demonstrated by analysis of gnomAD database showing LOEUF score of 0.19 for TNS3 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2a), citing Karczewski et al., 2020 and Lek et al., 2016 for gnomAD data.

claim: Integrin-β1 signaling is involved in survival of differentiating oligodendroglia.
source: Moreover, by conditional ablation of integrin-β1 in vivo, it was demonstrated that integrin-β1 signaling is involved in survival of differentiating oligodendroglia, but not required for axon ensheathment and myelination per se (Benninger et al., 2006).
evidence: Stated based on prior published work, citing Benninger et al., 2006.

claim: Integrin α6β1 association with Fyn kinase is required to amplify PDGF survival signaling in oligodendroglia.
source: In oligodendroglia, integrin α6β1 association with Fyn kinase is required to amplify PDGF survival signaling and promote myelin membrane formation by switching neuregulin signaling from a PI3K to a MAPK pathway (Colognato et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated based on prior published work, citing Colognato et al., 2004.

claim: Tns3 binds integrin-β1 through its phosphotyrosine-binding domain in fibroblasts.
source: Tensins are known to mediate integrin stabilization and activation in other cell types (Liao and Lo, 2021), with Tns3 been shown to bind integrin-β1 through its phosphotyrosine-binding domain and FAK through its SH2 domain in fibroblasts (Cui et al., 2004; Liao et al., 2007; Georgiadou et al., 2017).
evidence: Stated based on prior published work, citing Cui et al., 2004; Liao et al., 2007; Georgiadou et al., 2017; Liao and Lo, 2021.

claim: Oligodendrocyte precursor cells constitute a stable population of the postnatal and adult central nervous system.
source: Unlike most precursor cells, OPCs constitute a stable population of the postnatal and adult central nervous system (CNS) (Ffrench-Constant and Raff, 1986; Suzuki and Goldman, 2003).
evidence: Stated based on prior published work, citing Ffrench-Constant and Raff, 1986; Suzuki and Goldman, 2003.

claim: Demyelinated MS plaques can be normally repaired in early stages of the disease, presumably by endogenous OPCs.
source: Demyelinated MS plaques can be normally repaired in early stages of the disease, presumably by endogenous OPCs, but this repair process becomes increasingly inefficient with aging, when OPC differentiation seems to be partially impaired (Chang et al., 2002; Compston and Coles, 2002; Neumann et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated based on prior published work, citing Chang et al., 2002; Compston and Coles, 2002; Neumann et al., 2019.

claim: Oligodendrocytes play key roles during brain development by allowing saltatory conduction of myelinated axons.
source: Oligodendrocyte (OL) lineage cells, mainly constituted by oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) and OLs, play key roles during brain development and neuronal support by allowing saltatory conduction of myelinated axons and metabolically supporting these axons with lactate or glucose shuttling through the myelin sheath (Fünfschilling et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2012; Meyer et al., 2018).
evidence: Stated based on established knowledge, citing Fünfschilling et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2012; Meyer et al., 2018.

claim: Tns3 likely mediates integrin-β1 survival signaling to the actin cytoskeleton during oligodendrocyte differentiation.
source: Altogether, our findings reveal a specific time window during which transcriptional upregulation of Tns3 in immature OLs is required for OL differentiation likely by mediating integrin-β1 survival signaling to the actin cytoskeleton as OL undergo the large morphological changes required for their terminal differentiation.
evidence: Inferred from multiple lines of evidence including Tns3 co-expression with integrin-β1, known Tns3 binding to integrin-β1 and actin, and phenotypes of Tns3 deletion resembling integrin-β1 deletion.
